symptom: On a multi-language project `describe navigation` / `describe menu` printed a menu item's caption in whichever language was stored first, while `describe page` prints the same kind of text in the project's default language; and an item whose caption read empty and whose action was not a page (an icon-only microflow item) was missing from describe entirely, so a describe -> exec round trip deleted it.
cause: The navigation reader had its own text rule, `textOf` = the first non-empty Texts$Translation in document order, instead of the page rule (selectTranslationText: the default language even when empty, else en_US, else the first non-empty); and navMenuItemFromGen returned nil for an item with an empty caption, no page and no sub-items (a legacy-reader filter).
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/navigation_read.go` (`textOf` now calls `model.SelectTranslation` with `model.AuthoringLanguage()`; the filter in `navMenuItemFromGen` is gone); the executor resolves the language before reading (`describeDefaultLanguage` / `authoringLanguage` in describeNavigation, listNavigationMenu, describeMenu, execCreateNavigation, execCreateMenu)
insight: A translatable text has ONE read rule (model.SelectTranslation) and ONE write rule (bsonnav.SetTextsTextTranslation); a per-document copy drifts, and the drift only shows on a project whose default language is not the first one stored. Because the backend reads the language through the process-level model.AuthoringLanguage, every executor path that reads captions must call describeDefaultLanguage(ctx) first — a test that mocks GetNavigation and records the language seen at call time catches a missing call. A reader filter that drops an element is a delete on the next rewrite: compare the elements read with the elements stored.
